title: Cross-environment access decision guidelines and IAM mapping
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a lightweight decision guide and working IAM mapping for RBAC v2 that covers the three hosting tiers (hosted API, Dedicated, Private). Goal: give engineer-facing, actionable rules for scoping roles, templates for common policies, and a minimal SIEM/audit export contract for evidence automation.

Intended audience:
- Eng infra (platform-engineering, serving-runtime)
- Security/compliance reviewers
- Solutions engineering when onboarding customers

High-level decision flow (quick):
1) Is the access for a human or for a machine/service? -> humans get short-lived non-service accounts + 2FA, machines get service accounts or workload identities.
2) Which environment? -> hosted | dedicated | private. If private, prefer customer-managed KMS and restrict access to control plane roles only.
3) Is the action control-plane (configs, rollouts) or data-plane (model inference, logs)? -> separate role families.
4) Least-privilege by default; start with read-only and elevate via canary-approved PRs.

Role matrix (compact, rows = role family):
- platform-viewer: read-only control plane, no secret access, can view model catalog and per-route dashboards
- platform-operator: manage deployments, trigger rollouts, can escalate to emergency rollback, limited to team namespace or tenant id
- infra-admin: create/rotate service accounts, manage autoscaling groups; should be scoped to org or Dedicated cluster only
- billing-auditor: read-only usage and billing reporting, no deployment perms
- tenant-admin (for Dedicated/private): tenant-scoped role, can manage tenant-specific keys, onboarding flows, and service mapping
- svc-inference-worker: service account used by inference pods; minimal IAM to read model artifacts and write inference logs to tenant logs path

Example policy templates (shortened, apply variables like ${TENANT_ID}):
- Read-only control-plane policy (JSON-ish):
  - allow: ["controlplane.routes.get","controlplane.models.list","controlplane.metrics.read"]
  - deny: ["controlplane.keys.*","controlplane.secrets.*"]

- Scoped deployment operator:
  - allow: ["deployments.create:${NAMESPACE}", "deployments.update:${NAMESPACE}", "rollouts.trigger:${NAMESPACE}"]
  - conditions: resource.namespace == ${NAMESPACE} AND request.origin in ${TRUSTED_SUBNETS}

- Service account for inference (least set):
  - allow: ["models.fetch:${MODEL_PATH}", "kvcache.read:${CACHE_BUCKET}"], ttl-bound key material, IP-restrictable for Dedicated

Environment-specific rules (notes and gotchas):
- Hosted API:
  - No customer-level access to control plane. Support personnel get scoped read-only views via platform-viewer with ephemeral session tokens.
  - SIEM ingestion must tag tenant_id for cross-tenant suspicious activity detection.

- Dedicated:
  - Operators from customer side can get tenant-admin roles limited to their cluster region. We require role-approval PRs and evidence collection of justification.
  - For rotation, customer requests are executed via automation pipeline that records a rotation run event (see SIEM contract).

- Private (VPC/on-prem):
  - Control plane access usually via customer-managed VPN; Redwood assigns 'private-control-plane-proxy' role for agents.
  - We do not store customer keys in hosted KMS by default — document explicit exceptions.

SIEM / audit export contract (minimal fields to include in every exported event):
- event_id (string, UUID)
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- service (e.g., "controlplane", "inference", "rotation-run")
- actor_type (human|service)
- actor_id (email or service-account id)
- actor_role (one of role identifiers)
- action (string, canonical verb e.g., "deploy.create", "secrets.rotate")
- resource_type (e.g., "deployment","model","key")
- resource_id (string)
- env (hosted|dedicated|private)
- tenant_id (if applicable)
- outcome (success|failure|denied)
- request_id / trace_id
- change_summary (short text; for config changes include before/after diff id)
- evidence_refs (list of evidence artifact ids or s3 paths)

Notes on export format and retention:
- Exports must be newline-delimited JSON. For hosted, include tenant_id; for private, tenant_id is optional but network-origin must be populated.
- Retention defaults: 90 days hot, 1 year cold. For customers with compliance needs we support extended retention add-on.

Evidence automation: recommended minimal pipeline
1) Event capture hook (control plane + infra agents) -> writes event to internal event-bus (kafka) with full event payload.
2) Evidence aggregator service picks high-risk events (policy: deploy.*, secrets.*, role.grant) and stores a zipped evidence bundle in evidence-bucket/${TENANT_ID}/${event_id}.zip. Bundle components: audit.log, request-body.json, config-diff.patch, operator-approval.md
3) SIEM export consumer reads event and pushes to centralized ES/Datadog/Splunk index; export also pushes a proof-of-storing pointer into the event (evidence_refs).
4) Automated verification job runs nightly: sample 1% of high-risk bundles and verifies signature/hash against chain-of-trust key (KMS). Failures emit SEC tickets automatically.

Quick commands / snippets (for ops):
- Create tenant-scoped operator policy (pseudo):
  ./iamctl create-policy --name tenant-operator-${TENANT_ID} --allow "deployments.*:${TENANT_ID}" --condition "namespace==${TENANT_ID}"

- Evidence bundle upload (pseudo):
  zip -r ${EVENT_ID}.zip audit.log request.json diff.patch approval.md && aws s3 cp ${EVENT_ID}.zip s3://evidence-bucket/${TENANT_ID}/${EVENT_ID}.zip --acl bucket-owner-full-control

Open questions / TODOs (triage this list):
- How to represent partial-deny conditions in a way that downstream SIEMs can compute (currently some fields are embedded in nested policy expressions; we should flatten).
- Define exact TTLs for service-account keys in Dedicated clusters vs Private (customer-managed). Proposal: 1h default for short-lived tokens, 7d maximum for long-lived service accounts with rotation automation.
- Formalize mapping of 'actor_role' canonical list to existing role ids in the RBAC v2 protobuf. (Jira: SEC-456)

Next steps and owners:
- Draft policy proto -> Ravi (by 2026-02-28)
- Implement evidence-bundle zipper in infra repo -> Liam (PR ready by 2026-03-10)
